batch_node.name: aws_core pages v0.3.0
batch_node.description: aws_core's reusable pages (req-aws-core-page-dashboard, -organization, -network): /aws, a dashboard of count tiles, the estate as one picture and two tables; /aws/organization, the OU tree placed by layout tags, with SCP attachments and account placement; /aws/network, transit gateways, attachments, gateways, firewalls and Direct Connect. Every search reads whatever AWS nodes the grid holds: nothing here names a deployment. The children nest under /aws by URL. The graphs share one layout module (aws-estate.js) and the tiles are the aws-counts panel type. v0.2.0 (George, 2026-09-24): the organization graph draws the OU tree only, laid out by aws-organization.js from the nodes' layout:* tags; its scoped, scp and idp searches are gone (on an existing grid, retire those three search nodes: a batch cannot remove a node). v0.3.0 (George, 2026-09-24): the network graph nests each VPC's subnets in it, one column per availability zone, with its internet gateway beside them and a NAT gateway inside its subnet, from PARTITIONED_INTO_SUBNET, ATTACHED_TO_VPC and RESIDES_IN_SUBNET; a subnets table lists each VPC's subnets with zone and CIDR.

node.name: AWS counts
node.description: Count tiles over the AWS estate: accounts, OUs, SCPs, VPCs, internet gateways (public front doors and egress exits), internet-facing load balancers, buckets not blocking public access, network firewalls, transit gateways and their attachments, KMS keys, and the accounts inside each compliance boundary. Amber marks a count worth a second look; 'design' marks a count made only of planned nodes.

node.name: AWS estate
node.description: The AWS estate in one picture: the organisation tree (every OU as a box around its accounts), each transit gateway around its attachments with a line to every VPC it attaches, the VPCs, gateways and firewalls, and the compliance boundaries each OU is scoped to.

node.name: AWS estate projection
node.description: AWS estate: one elevation, the aws-estate layout module, standard icon-badge chrome, opens fitted.

node.name: AWS estate elevation
node.description: AWS estate at one elevation.

node.name: AWS estate layout
node.description: aws-estate.js: nests the organisation tree on NESTED_UNDER_PARENT and each transit gateway's attachments on ATTACHED_TO_TRANSIT_GATEWAY; every other edge is a line; roots stack in bands (organisation, transit, VPCs and gateways, policies, boundaries, outside systems).

node.name: aws — AWS estate nodes
node.description: Every organisation, OU, account, transit gateway, attachment, VPC, internet gateway, NAT gateway and network firewall on the grid.

node.name: aws — AWS estate nested
node.description: The organisation tree: each account and OU under its parent (NESTED_UNDER_PARENT).

node.name: aws — AWS estate scoped
node.description: Compliance boundaries scoped from an OU or an account (SCOPED_TO_COMPLIANCE_BOUNDARY), with the boundary node.

node.name: aws — AWS estate tgw
node.description: Each transit gateway attachment on its gateway.

node.name: aws — AWS estate attaches
node.description: Each VPC attachment and the VPC it connects.

node.name: Accounts per OU
node.description: How many accounts sit directly in each OU (NESTED_UNDER_PARENT).

node.name: aws — Accounts per OU
node.description: How many accounts sit directly in each OU (NESTED_UNDER_PARENT).

query: RETURN o.name AS ou, count(a) AS accounts

node.name: Boundary scope
node.description: What each compliance boundary is scoped from: the OUs (and any accounts) with a SCOPED_TO_COMPLIANCE_BOUNDARY edge to it. Everything under a scoped OU is inside.

columns.title: Scoped from
columns.header_tooltip: The OU or account the boundary is scoped from.

node.name: aws — Boundary scope
node.description: What each compliance boundary is scoped from: the OUs (and any accounts) with a SCOPED_TO_COMPLIANCE_BOUNDARY edge to it. Everything under a scoped OU is inside.

query: RETURN b.name AS boundary, x.name AS scoped_from, x.entity_type AS kind

node.name: AWS
node.description: The AWS dashboard: count tiles over the estate, the estate as one picture (organisation tree, transit gateways and their attachments, VPCs and gateways, boundaries), accounts per OU and what each compliance boundary is scoped from. The organization and network pages go deeper.

node.name: AWS organization
node.description: The AWS Organizations tree: the organization (its root) around every top-level OU and account, each OU around its children. Placement is read from each node's layout tags (layout:column, layout:order, layout:fill); service control policies, compliance boundaries and Identity Center are left to the tables and the other pages.

node.name: AWS organization projection
node.description: AWS organization: one elevation, the aws-organization layout module, standard icon-badge chrome, opens fitted.

node.name: AWS organization elevation
node.description: AWS organization at one elevation.

node.name: AWS organization layout
node.description: aws-organization.js: nests the organisation tree on NESTED_UNDER_PARENT; the organization lays its children out in columns, each OU its children in one row, both ordered by the nodes' layout tags; layout:fill boxes stretch to their column or row.

node.name: aws — AWS organization nodes
node.description: Every organization, OU and account on the grid.

node.name: aws — AWS organization nested
node.description: The organisation tree: each account and OU under its parent (NESTED_UNDER_PARENT).

node.name: SCP attachments
node.description: Every service control policy and each OU, account or root it is attached to (ATTACHED_TO_TARGET). A policy attached to an OU bounds everything under it.

columns.title: Attached to
columns.header_tooltip: The OU, account or organization root.

node.name: aws — SCP attachments
node.description: Every service control policy and each OU, account or root it is attached to (ATTACHED_TO_TARGET). A policy attached to an OU bounds everything under it.

query: RETURN p.name AS policy, t.name AS target, t.entity_type AS target_kind, p.data.description AS description

node.name: Account placement
node.description: Every account and the OU (or organization root) it sits directly under.

columns.title: Parent
columns.header_tooltip: The OU or organization it sits directly under.

columns.title: Account id
columns.header_tooltip: Blank until the account exists (a design account has none).

node.name: aws — Account placement
node.description: Every account and the OU (or organization root) it sits directly under.

query: RETURN a.name AS account, p.name AS parent, a.data.account_id AS account_id

node.name: Organization
node.description: The AWS Organizations structure: the OU tree with its accounts, service control policy attachments, the compliance boundaries each OU is scoped to, and the identity provider IAM Identity Center trusts.

node.name: AWS network
node.description: The network plane: each transit gateway around its attachments, a line from every VPC attachment to its VPC; each VPC around its subnets (one column per availability zone, public subnets on top) with its internet gateway beside them; a NAT gateway inside the one subnet it sits in, and a resource spread over several subnets (a network firewall's endpoints) inside the VPC with a line to each. A VPC with no attachment is not on any transit gateway (a tenant VPC, or a public front door).

node.name: AWS network projection
node.description: AWS network: one elevation, the aws-estate layout module, standard icon-badge chrome, opens fitted.

node.name: AWS network elevation
node.description: AWS network at one elevation.

node.name: AWS network layout
node.description: aws-estate.js: nests each transit gateway's attachments on ATTACHED_TO_TRANSIT_GATEWAY, each VPC's subnets on PARTITIONED_INTO_SUBNET and its internet gateway on ATTACHED_TO_VPC, and what resides in one subnet inside it; every other edge is a line; roots stack in bands.

node.name: aws — AWS network nodes
node.description: Every transit gateway, attachment, VPC, subnet, internet gateway, NAT gateway and network firewall on the grid.

node.name: aws — AWS network tgw
node.description: Each transit gateway attachment on its gateway.

node.name: aws — AWS network attaches
node.description: Each VPC attachment and the VPC it connects.

node.name: aws — AWS network peers
node.description: Each peering attachment and its peer transit gateway.

node.name: Transit gateway attachments
node.description: Every VPC attachment: its transit gateway, the VPC it connects and that VPC's CIDR. A VPC missing here is not on any transit gateway.

columns.title: Transit gateway
columns.header_tooltip: The gateway the attachment belongs to.

columns.title: CIDR
columns.header_tooltip: The VPC's CIDR block; blank until assigned.

node.name: aws — Transit gateway attachments
node.description: Every VPC attachment: its transit gateway, the VPC it connects and that VPC's CIDR. A VPC missing here is not on any transit gateway.

query: RETURN g.name AS transit_gateway, a.name AS attachment, v.name AS vpc, v.data.cidr_block AS cidr

node.name: Internet gateways
node.description: Every internet gateway: each one is a path to or from the internet (a public front door or an egress exit) and should be a documented exception.

node.name: aws — Internet gateways
node.description: Every internet gateway: each one is a path to or from the internet (a public front door or an egress exit) and should be a documented exception.

node.description: Direct Connect connections, virtual interfaces and gateways into a transit gateway.

config.text: No Direct Connect connection is on the grid. When one is, this section lists each connection, its virtual interfaces and the Direct Connect gateway associated with a transit gateway.

node.name: Network
node.description: The AWS network plane: transit gateways and their VPC attachments, each VPC's subnets by zone, the VPCs' internet gateways, NAT gateways and network firewalls, and Direct Connect.

node.name: Subnets
node.description: Every subnet a VPC is partitioned into: the VPC, the subnet, its availability zone, CIDR and whether it is public. Blank CIDRs are not yet assigned.

columns.title: CIDR
columns.header_tooltip: The subnet's CIDR block; blank until assigned.

columns.title: Public

node.name: aws — Subnets
node.description: Every subnet a VPC is partitioned into: the VPC, the subnet, its availability zone, CIDR and whether it is public. Blank CIDRs are not yet assigned.

query: RETURN v.name AS vpc, s.name AS subnet, s.data.availability_zone AS zone, s.data.cidr_block AS cidr, s.data.public AS public
